concepts.description: Limits describe the value a function approaches near a point, and continuity means a function's limit at a point equals its value there. These ideas are the foundation for everything else in the course.
concepts.name: Limits and Continuity

concepts.description: The derivative measures the instantaneous rate of change of a function, computed with rules such as the power, product, quotient, and chain rules. It is the core computational tool of the course.
concepts.name: Derivatives and Differentiation Rules

concepts.description: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links differentiation and integration, showing that integrals can be evaluated using antiderivatives. It unifies the two main halves of the course.
concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

concepts.description: Riemann sums approximate the area under a curve by summing rectangles, and taking the limit gives the definite integral. This is the conceptual definition of integration.
concepts.name: Riemann Sums

concepts.description: Methods such as substitution, integration by parts, and partial fractions are used to find antiderivatives that are not immediately obvious. These techniques make the Fundamental Theorem usable in practice.
concepts.name: Techniques of Integration

concepts.description: Definite integrals are used to compute areas between curves and volumes of solids, such as by disk, washer, or shell methods. These applications show how integration models real geometric quantities.
concepts.name: Applications of Integration to Area and Volume

concepts.description: Implicit differentiation finds derivatives of relations where y is not explicitly solved in terms of x. It extends differentiation to curves defined by equations.
concepts.name: Implicit Differentiation

concepts.description: Optimization uses derivatives to find maximum and minimum values of a function on an interval or in a practical setting. It is a major application of the derivative.
concepts.name: Optimization

concepts.description: Related rates problems use implicit differentiation with respect to time to relate the rates of change of connected quantities. They apply differentiation to changing physical situations.
concepts.name: Related Rates

concepts.description: Curve sketching uses first and second derivatives to identify increasing and decreasing intervals, concavity, and extrema, producing an accurate graph of a function.
concepts.name: Curve Sketching

concepts.description: The Mean Value Theorem guarantees a point where the instantaneous rate of change equals the average rate of change over an interval. It is a key theoretical result behind many derivative-based arguments.
concepts.name: Mean Value Theorem

concepts.description: L'Hopital's Rule evaluates limits of indeterminate forms such as 0/0 or infinity/infinity by differentiating numerator and denominator. It extends the reach of limit techniques.
concepts.name: L'Hopital's Rule

concepts.description: Differential equations relate a function to its derivatives, and basic methods such as separation of variables solve simple cases. They model growth, decay, and other change processes.
concepts.name: Differential Equations Basics

concepts.description: Sequences are ordered lists of numbers, and series are sums of their terms, studied through convergence tests. Series such as power series extend calculus to infinite processes.
concepts.name: Sequences and Series
